title: Reconfigurable field-free spin Hall nano-oscillators enabled by crystallographic anisotropy in epitaxial Co/Pt
authors: Jong-Guk Choi, Avinash Kumar Chaurasiya, Jaimin Kang, Venkatesh Vadde, Peter G. Lim, Roman Khymyn, Ahmad A. Awad, Akash Kumar, Mark C. Hersam, Vinayak P. Dravid, Pedram Khalili Amiri, Johan Åkerman
abstract: Spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) are nanoscale microwave sources for wireless communication, neuromorphic computing and oscillator-based Ising machines, but conventional devices require a global magnetic bias. Here we replace this bias through crystallographic anisotropy in epitaxial Co/Pt. Growth of hcp Co with its c-axis in the film plane produces an anisotropy field of about 0.36 T and enables field-free auto-oscillations above 10 GHz in nanoconstriction SHNOs. The active current polarity is selected by the remanent magnetization, providing nonvolatile reconfiguration of the oscillation state. Micro-focused Brillouin light scattering confirms that the nonlinear response is confined to the nanoconstriction region. Lithographic control of the angle between the current and anisotropy axes tunes the excitation threshold and drives two spectral branches from separated modes to a dominant single branch, consistent with mutual synchronization. These results establish epitaxial crystallographic anisotropy as a route to reconfigurable field-free spintronic oscillators and oscillator networks.
summary: This work introduces a novel spintronic device architecture using epitaxial Co/Pt films to create reconfigurable, field-free spin Hall nano-oscillators. By exploiting the large, intrinsic magnetic anisotropy derived from crystal growth, the device achieves stable, high-frequency auto-oscillations at zero applied field. This establishes crystallographic anisotropy as a powerful, non-volatile material design rule for next-generation spintronic oscillators.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop reconfigurable, field-free spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) to overcome the limitation of requiring a global external magnetic bias for operation.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that utilizing the intrinsic crystallographic anisotropy of epitaxial Co/Pt bilayers can generate a sufficient internal magnetic bias, enabling stable, high-frequency auto-oscillations above 10 GHz without external fields.
method: The research combines advanced experimental techniques, including Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (STFMR) and micro-focused Brillouin Light Scattering ($\mu$-BLS), with micromagnetic simulations.
model_or_system: The system involves epitaxial Co/Pt bilayers grown on MgO(110), where the crystallographic anisotropy of the hexagonal Co layer dictates the magnetic easy axis and provides the necessary internal field. The device is patterned into nano-constrictions for localized spin dynamics.
key_observables: Field-free auto-oscillation frequency (>10 GHz), nonvolatile reconfiguration of active current polarity based on remanent magnetization, and the tuning of excitation thresholds via the angle between the current and anisotropy axes.
important_parameters: Anisotropy field ($	ext{B}_{	ext{ani}}$) $\approx 0.36 	ext{ T}$; oscillation frequency $>10 	ext{ GHz}$; current angle ($\phi_I$) dependence of the threshold current.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the preservation and utilization of the large, intrinsic crystallographic anisotropy established during the epitaxial growth process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the epitaxial alignment and anisotropy confirmation via hysteresis loops, show STFMR spectra confirming field-free oscillations dependent on remanent magnetization, and use $\mu$-BLS to map the spatial confinement and angular tuning of the oscillation modes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the material system and confirming the large anisotropy field (via hysteresis/STFMR) to demonstrating field-free auto-oscillations. It then details the control mechanisms, showing how the current angle tunes the excitation threshold and induces mode synchronization, culminating in the establishment of this anisotropy as a design principle.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the concept of using intrinsic material symmetries (crystallographic anisotropy) to engineer non-equilibrium, coherent dynamics (auto-oscillations) without external driving fields shares conceptual parallels with engineering quantum states using engineered Hamiltonians or boundary conditions in AMO physics.
